subject: [PATCH] memcg: Don't call schedule_work when no spinning is allowed

reviews.author: David Stevens
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David Stevens noted that he found the issue via code inspection and was unable to trigger it in real-world scenarios, except by writing a hacky driver using alloc_pages_nolock(). He suggested instead of adding complexity, simply returning if spinning is not allowed on the done_restock path.

Reviewer David Stevens noted that returning from the done_restock path without triggering memcg reclaim could lead to missing MEMCG_HIGH events, which he considers a more serious issue than dropping userspace notifications.
reviews.raw_body:
I just found this via code inspection. I spent a little bit trying to
trigger it for real, but the only way I managed was by writing a hacky
driver absuing alloc_pages_nolock().

---

There would be no guarantee that memcg reclaim would ever be
triggered, which also would also stop MEMCG_HIGH events from being
generated. Overall that seems a more serious than just dropping
userspace notifications like is done for MEMCG_MAX.

That said, it is very much an edge case. I can send a patch with the
simpler fix if dropping the events is preferred.

-David

2026-08-31.patch_summary: This patch modifies the memcg (memory cgroup) code to prevent unnecessary work scheduling when spinning is not allowed, simplifying the done_restock code path by returning early instead of adding complexity.

reviews.author: Michal Hocko
reviews.summary: Reviewer Michal Hocko suggested simplifying the code by returning immediately on the done_restock path instead of adding complexity, implying that the current approach is too complicated and may not be necessary.
reviews.raw_body:
Yes, let's go simpler before making this more complex without any actual
user.

-- 
Michal Hocko
SUSE Labs

reviews.author: Johannes Weiner
reviews.summary: reviewer prefers a simple return statement over more complex code, citing concerns about indefinite errors and potential future issues
reviews.raw_body:
I'm leaning that way too. It's an indefinite error, and it's a freely
programmable surface.

IMO, a few lines of relatively straight-forward, self-explanatory code
is better than code that needs a comment and leaves a problem that
somebody in the future might run into.

reviews.author: Michal Hocko
reviews.summary: Reviewer Michal Hocko expressed skepticism about the need for NMI-safe charges, pointing out that they are rare and temporary discrepancies due to userspace running.
reviews.raw_body:
I am really curious about the indefinite error side of things. It has
been my understanding that these NMI safe charges are a) rare and b)
there is userspace running so eventually any discrepancies would
resolve so the excess is temporary.

-- 
Michal Hocko
SUSE Labs

reviews.author: David Stevens
reviews.summary: Reviewer David Stevens pointed out that the patch's assumption about the done_restock code path being the only way to hit the issue is incorrect, and provided an alternative scenario where bpf_arena_alloc_pages() can also trigger this condition.
reviews.raw_body:
I spent a bit longer looking, and this can be hit via bpf_arena_alloc_pages().

-David

reviews.author: Johannes Weiner
reviews.summary: Reviewer Johannes Weiner expressed concern that the patch's approach to handling the !allow_spinning case is overly reliant on the 'luck of the common case', and suggested adding working code instead of a lengthy comment.
reviews.raw_body:
So I think the question is what limits the error in both space and
time. When you say it's rare and userspace fixes it, it basically
means the answer is: luck of the common case.

But that doesn't help the worst case that can be triggered.

Like I said, if we need to have code to handle that !allow_spinning
case anyway, I'd rather just have a few lines of working code than a
(lengthy) comment explaining the luck of the common case.

2026-09-01.patch_summary: This patch modifies the memcg (memory cgroup) code to prevent unnecessary work scheduling when spinning is not allowed, simplifying the done_restock code path by returning early instead of adding complexity.
